items.sum_en: Officials who have created environmental destruction in the name of redevelopment around Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park, which is like the lungs of Greater Hyderabad. In the name of change in the alignment of the project, they are ready to attack the greenery in another corridor. In the backdrop of the steel bridge work to be undertaken from Mugdha Junction to Panjagutta NFCL Corridor, the 4.3 km central median has been lush green for decades. A large number of trees were uprooted.
items.sum_te: గ్రేటర్‌ హైదరాబాద్‌కు ఊపిరితిత్తుల్లాంటి కాసు బ్రహ్మానందరెడ్డి  జాతీయ పారు చుట్టూ మళ్లీ అభివృద్ధి పేరిట పర్యావరణ విధ్వంసం సృష్టించిన అధికారులు. ప్రాజెక్టు అలైన్‌మెంట్‌ మార్పు పేరిట మరో కారిడార్‌లో పచ్చదనంపై వేటు వేసేందుకు సిద్ధమయ్యారు. ముగ్ధ జంక్షన్‌ నుంచి పంజాగుట్ట ఎన్‌ఎఫ్‌సీఎల్‌ కారిడార్‌ వరకు చేపట్టనున్న స్టీల్‌ బ్రిడ్జి పనుల నేపథ్యంలో 4.3 కిలోమీటర్ల సెంట్రల్‌ మీడియన్‌లో దశాబ్దాలుగా కళకళలాడుతున్న పచ్చదనం. పెద్ద ఎత్తున చెట్లు నేలకూలే ప్రమాదం ఏర్పడింది.

items.sum_en: 20 years after a Washington state dam was slated for demolition, 1,100 acres of ecosystem along the Lower Elwha River is recovering, having lain muddy and dormant under the dam’s engorged reservoir for more than a century. 114 years after it was flooded, the Lower Elwha Klallam tribe is just a signature away from having 1,100 acres of land returned to them.

items.sum_en: In the fourth T20 international match against India in Hyderabad, West Indies captain Shai Hope impressed with his amazing batting. Along with his unbeaten 102 off 50 balls, Muthoot received the Fincorp Golden Player of the Match award. West Indies won the match by 24 runs and leveled the five-match series 2-2 at the Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium. Hope hit four fours and nine sixes in his innings. Apart from scoring 102 off 50 balls at a strike rate of 204, he was instrumental in the WestIndies scoring 247 for the loss of three wickets in 20 overs. India were limited to 223 runs in chasing down the target.

items.title: A 47-year study reveals the age when your body starts losing strength

items.title: Teen Triathlete Raises More Than $30,000 to Donate Bikes and Riding Lessons to Low-Income Families
items.summary: Continuing GNN’s coverage of youth nonprofit leaders, the Pedal Forward Foundation in Georgia has distributed hundreds of bicycles to low income families, and taught hundreds of children how to ride them. It’s founder,…
items.sum_en: Continuing GNN’s coverage of youth nonprofit leaders, the Pedal Forward Foundation in Georgia has distributed hundreds of bicycles to low income families, and taught hundreds of children how to ride them. It’s founder, Jonathan Thai, was inspired to step up and serve his community after the local REI closed down a community bike-riding workshop. items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious

items.sum_en: A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

items.title: This tiny jurassic predator helped pave the way for the human brain
items.summary: A 165-million-year-old fossil has revealed an extraordinary Jurassic predator that may help explain how mammals developed one of their most important evolutionary advantages. Although only 20 inches long, Megacauda…
items.sum_en: A 165-million-year-old fossil has revealed an extraordinary Jurassic predator that may help explain how mammals developed one of their most important evolutionary advantages. Although only 20 inches long, Megacauda sungei was a heavyweight among early mammal relatives, swimming through ancient waterways and hunting prey with specialized teeth. Its advanced swallowing anatomy reveals an early step toward the ability to safely nurse on milk, a key development in mammalian evolution.

items.title: Scientists uncover the 2.3-billion-year-old secret that helped keep Earth habitable
items.summary: Scientists may have solved a 2.3-billion-year-old mystery about how Earth maintained enough oxygen to support life. Ancient rocks reveal that phosphorus recycling in the oceans created a self-sustaining cycle that…
items.sum_en: Scientists may have solved a 2.3-billion-year-old mystery about how Earth maintained enough oxygen to support life. Ancient rocks reveal that phosphorus recycling in the oceans created a self-sustaining cycle that helped keep oxygen levels high, even as the planet underwent dramatic environmental changes. The discovery challenges assumptions about Earth's early atmosphere and raises new questions about why complex life took so long to emerge.

items.title: Scientists discover vanilla’s hidden healing potential

items.sum_en: Scientists have discovered that vanillin, the compound that gives vanilla its distinctive flavor, has powerful properties that could help fight infections, reduce inflammation, and promote wound healing. The inexpensive, widely available ingredient could one day become an important component of advanced wound treatments and regenerative medicine.

items.sum_en: Scientists are reporting that a simple adjustment to how people walk can relieve knee arthritis pain as effectively as prescription drugs—while also slowing the deterioration of cartilage. Nearly a quarter of people over the age of 40 experience painful osteoarthritis, due to degrading joint-cushioning cartilage—and there is currently no way of reversing this damage.

items.title: Scientists make stunning discovery that could help explain why life exists
items.summary: Scientists have discovered that the universe's fundamental physical constants may be finely balanced to make life possible. Even tiny changes to these constants could make liquids too thick or too thin for essential…
items.sum_en: Scientists have discovered that the universe's fundamental physical constants may be finely balanced to make life possible. Even tiny changes to these constants could make liquids too thick or too thin for essential biological processes, potentially preventing life as we know it. Surprisingly, these life-friendly conditions existed billions of years before living cells appeared. The findings raise intriguing questions about why the laws of physics seem so well suited to life.

items.title: Giant Tortoise Population is Thriving–Survey Finds 180,000 on One Island Chain
items.summary: A landmark survey of the world’s largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has revealed the once-endangered species is now thriving. The latest count of tortoises on the Seychelles atoll of Aldabra revealed that…
items.sum_en: A landmark survey of the world’s largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has revealed the once-endangered species is now thriving. The latest count of tortoises on the Seychelles atoll of Aldabra revealed that there are approximately 180,000 living on the islands. The world’s largest free-roaming giant tortoise population is now thriving, with over 180,000 counted on Aldabra atoll in the Seychelles.
